title: B-PER Lysis Protocol
author: Ken Christensen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bmg6k3ze

steps.title: Centrifuge cells to form pellet
steps.instruction: Spin the bacterial culture at 5,000 × g in a tared tube for 10 minutes to pellet the cells.

steps.title: Decant supernatant and weigh pellet
steps.instruction: Decant the spent LB medium, then determine and record the mass of the wet cell pellet.

steps.title: Freeze cell pellet for storage
steps.instruction: Freeze the pellet either overnight at –20 °C or rapidly in liquid nitrogen; keep frozen until needed.

steps.title: Thaw pellet at room temperature
steps.instruction: When ready to proceed, thaw the frozen pellet at room temperature.

steps.title: Add B-PER reagent and homogenize
steps.instruction: Add 4 mL of B‑PER Reagent per gram of wet cell pellet. Pipette the suspension up and down until it is homogeneous.

steps.title: Add optional lysozyme and DNase I
steps.instruction: Optionally add 2 µL of lysozyme and 2 µL of DNase I for each 1 mL of B‑PER reagent added.

steps.title: Incubate lysate at room temperature
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture for 15 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate to separate proteins
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at approximately 15,000 × g for 5 minutes to separate soluble proteins from insoluble material. Note: a large amount of target protein remaining in the pellet may indicate inclusion‑body formation.
